```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The `karma2d` package contains the methods of Pereira, Palm and Bayer (2026).
The scripts that regenerate the tables and figures of the article live in the
`analysis/` directory of the **source repository**
(<https://github.com/VitorBSP/2d_karma_package>). That directory is not part
of the installed package, because the full Monte Carlo study takes hours and
should never run during package checks. This vignette gives the exact
commands and, importantly, an honest summary of what could and could not be
reproduced. Nothing below is evaluated when the vignette is built.

## Setup

Clone the repository, install the package and run every command **from the
repository root**:

```{sh setup-commands, eval = FALSE}
git clone https://github.com/VitorBSP/2d_karma_package
cd 2d_karma_package
Rscript -e 'remotes::install_local(".")'
```

## Monte Carlo study (Section 4.1; Tables 1-3)

```{sh monte-carlo, eval = FALSE}
# Development / continuous integration: few replications, minutes
Rscript analysis/simulations/run_monte_carlo.R --mode=quick

# Full study: 10,000 replications per scenario, image sizes 10, 25 and 50
Rscript analysis/simulations/run_monte_carlo.R --mode=full --cores=8

# Summaries: mean, bias, MSE, skewness, kurtosis and coverage of the
# estimators, with a comparison against Tables 1-3 of the article
Rscript analysis/simulations/summarize_monte_carlo.R
```

The runner saves a checkpoint after each scenario (and image size), so an
interrupted `--mode=full` run can be resumed by repeating the same command.
Every replication uses its own random-number stream derived from the master
seed, so the results do not depend on `--cores`.

## NDVI application (Section 4.2.1; Tables 4-5, Figures 4-7)

```{sh ndvi, eval = FALSE}
Rscript analysis/ndvi/run_ndvi.R
```

It uses the `ndvi_paraiba` dataset shipped with the package. It fits the 2-D
KARMA and the Gaussian 2-D ARMA models on the Phase I window, computes the
prediction metrics, the anomaly detection results and the figures, and writes a
comparison with the published values.

## GRDI application (Section 4.2.2)

```{sh grdi, eval = FALSE}
Rscript analysis/grdi/run_grdi.R --input=PATH/TO/grdi.csv
```

This requires the GRDI CSV file, which is **not** in the repository.

## Reproduction status

The following observations were made when re-running the original code and
the new pipeline. They are reported as found; the causes of the
discrepancies that remain open are not known.

### Monte Carlo

* The parameter values in the original simulation scripts for
  KARMA(1,0) ($\alpha = 0.67$, $\phi = (0.31, 0.21, -0.15)$, $\varphi = 23$)
  and KARMA(0,1) ($\alpha = 0.12$, $\theta = (0.1, 0.02, -0.12)$,
  $\varphi = 11$) **differ from the values reported in Tables 1 and 2** of
  the article (which were taken from the NDVI and GRDI fits). KARMA(1,1)
  matches Table 3.
* The pipeline uses the values of the article's tables by default and keeps the
  values of the original scripts available as an alternative scenario set
  (`--scenario_set=legacy_scripts`).
* The original scripts did not compute coverage rates, so it is not known how
  the coverage figures of the article were obtained. The new pipeline computes
  coverage from the expected information, the observed information and the
  matrix used by the original code.

### NDVI, Table 4 (estimates and standard errors)

* The estimates of the 2-D KARMA(1,0) and Gaussian 2-D ARMA(0,1) models and
  their standard errors reproduce the article to within one unit of the last
  printed decimal, **except the standard error of the shape parameter**.
* The article's value 0.2855 is reproduced exactly only by the information
  matrix of the original code, which mixes the **expected** blocks for the
  $\gamma$ parameters with the **observed** $\varphi\varphi$ entry. The
  corrected expected information gives 0.356 and the observed information
  0.315 (see `vignette("model-theory")` for the corrected formulas).

### NDVI, Table 5 (prediction metrics)

* The KARMA calibration-area MAE, MSE and RMSLE reproduce.
* The SMAPE values, the full-scene KARMA metrics and **all** Gaussian metrics
  do **not** reproduce; for example the Gaussian calibration MAE is 0.0299
  when computed here versus 0.0612 published. Two hypotheses were tested and
  rejected: that the original scripts computed MAPE rather than SMAPE (it
  matches neither), and that the Gaussian model was an ARMA(1,1). The cause is
  unresolved.
* With the metrics as computed, the advantage of KARMA over the Gaussian
  model in prediction accuracy is much smaller than reported. In anomaly
  detection, on the other hand, the KARMA residuals recover the whole
  injected anomaly (recall 1.00, precision about 0.90) versus a recall of about
  0.79 for the Gaussian model.

### Model selection

The automated model selection (significance, then parsimony, then MSE)
selects the 2-D KARMA(1,0) model on the NDVI Phase I window, as in the
article.

### GRDI

The GRDI application is **not reproducible from the repository**: the input
file is missing and the crop extent was not recorded.

## Details

A detailed account, with the evidence for each statement above, is in
`docs/technical-audit.md` in the source repository.
